first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, and two inherited memories (memory_31, memory_86) directly support that simplifying onboarding lifts activation and completion for self-serve/SMB accounts—this is the most directly actionable, well-supported lever for the objective. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given the competitor's aggressive entry pricing, but that memory only documents short-term acquisition/revenue lift for price-sensitive SMBs, not sustained qualified-revenue quality; racing on price against an aggressive entrant risks attracting low-LTV, low-margin accounts and normalizing discounting, which cuts against 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue.' Given only one experiment slot, I verify memory_73 because it is highly consequential (competitive threat, risk of margin erosion) yet insufficiently supported for the current objective, and memory_86 because it is the most consequential support for the action I intend to run and its onboarding-completion claim should be checked against the current 4% decline before committing capacity. Referral incentives and enterprise sales-assist are lower urgency given this week's specific down-metrics, and activation_messaging is a plausible alternative but less structurally supported than fixing the onboarding funnel itself.

final.rationale: Verification confirmed memory_86: shortened onboarding drove +13% completion, -2.1 days time-to-value, and +3% 30-day retention — a genuinely durable, quality-preserving lift that directly addresses this quarter's onboarding-completion and activation declines. Verification also disconfirmed the naive reading of memory_73: the 40% SMB discount produced +31% signup and +18% qualified revenue short-term but -12% 30-day retention, meaning the acquired cohort largely fails to survive first renewal — explicitly flagged as not generalizable to sustainable growth. Racing the competitor's entry pricing with discounting would likely replicate that pattern: short-term revenue optics at the cost of long-term qualified revenue, which is the stated objective. Given onboarding and activation are both down this quarter and the onboarding lever is now confirmed with retention-positive evidence (unlike discounting), I commit the single experiment slot to simplify_onboarding at standard scale — large enough to read a clean effect on completion/activation, not so broad as to overcommit before replicating the confirmed result in the current cohort. This still carries some risk: exp_86 was run under different competitive/market conditions than today's price-war environment, and it doesn't address the SMB attrition to the competitor directly, so I flag downstream value risk and preserve uncertainty about whether onboarding fixes alone will hold share against aggressive entry pricing.
